<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I will write a comprehensive architecture.md based on the reviewed files.

Proposing a monolithic Spring Boot backend with a separate frontend. PostgreSQL will handle ticket persistence, and PgVector will manage vectors co-located with the database. H2 is reserved for testing only. Frontend framework choice remains an open question. Chunking strategy justification follows.

Ticket knowledge will be assembled from titles, descriptions, comments, and resolution notes into documents. Paragraph-based chunking with a maximum size cap is recommended. Fixed-size chunks would split tickets awkwardly, and semantic splitting adds unnecessary complexity. The approach converts each ticket section type into a knowledge document, then applies paragraph-based chunking.

Each ticket becomes one structured knowledge document. Paragraphs merge when small and split at sentence boundaries when oversized. A configurable token limit of roughly 500–800 keeps chunks manageable. Embedding model selection is still open between local Ollama and cloud services.

Spring AI will provide a pluggable embedding layer. Local models will serve as the default for development and CI to avoid secrets and API costs. Cloud providers will remain configurable for demo quality. The final provider choice is deferred until the user confirms.

Re-ingestion timing is unresolved. Both synchronous post-commit and asynchronous event-driven approaches are proposed as options.

The state machine will live in a domain service as the single source of truth. Integration tests will cover its behavior.

Database, Spring AI, RAG parameters, embedding model, and generation LLM settings will all be driven by application.yml or environment variables.

Error handling will use @ControllerAdvice to ensure stable JSON responses per api-standards. The frontend will call the backend directly via REST rather than adding a BFF layer. CORS is noted as a local development implementation detail. Docker Compose may optionally run PostgreSQL alongside the application, but no deployment requirements are invented.
</details></think>

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

Created **`spec/architecture.md`** (draft) from [`spec/requirements.md`](spec/requirements.md), [`docs/assessment-brief.md`](docs/assessment-brief.md), `rules/` / `.cursor/rules/`, and `skills/documentation/SKILL.md`. No application code or migrations.

### What it covers

- **Context & principles** — monolithic Spring Boot + SPA, DB as source of truth, vector index as derived data, grounded single-step RAG (no agent).
- **System diagram** — UI → REST → ticket services / state machine / RAG → PostgreSQL, vector store, optional LLM & embedding providers via Spring AI.
- **Stack** — Java 21, Spring Boot 3, Spring AI, PostgreSQL, PgVector preferred (Chroma noted as PDF example), React/Next TBD, REST under `/api/...`.
- **Backend layering** — `api`, `domain`, `service`, `persistence`, `ai`/`rag`, `config`; where the state machine and re-ingestion sit.
- **Frontend** — surfaces tied to FRs; errors from stable JSON; API base URL via env.
- **Persistence** — relational tickets/comments; vector metadata (`ticketId`, status, priority, assignee, category); re-ingest on update/close.
- **RAG (required depth)**  
  - **Chunking:** paragraph/comment-based with configurable max size; semantic splitting out of scope initially; justified in §9.3.  
  - **Embeddings:** Spring AI–swappable; local/Ollama for dev/CI vs optional cloud; same model at ingest and query; tradeoffs in §9.4.  
  - **Retrieval:** configurable top-K + threshold; no LLM call when nothing passes threshold.
- **State machine** — domain-only enforcement; repos must not bypass; 409/400 per future API contract.
- **Configuration, errors, security** — aligns with `api-standards`; auth explicitly not assumed.

### Open questions (§15)

Fifteen items are listed for later specs/confirmation (ticket ID format, full API/ask schemas, auth, H2 scope, frontend choice, transition API, skipped transitions, re-ingest sync vs async, LLM default, migrations, etc.) — nothing invented as product fact.

### Suggested next specs

`data-model.md`, `api-contract.md`, `state-machine.md`, `rag-ingestion.md`, and `rag-api-contract.md` are referenced as the natural follow-ons.

If you want changes before those (e.g. lock in PgVector + Next.js, or prefer Chroma), say which open questions to resolve and we can update the architecture doc accordingly.
